title: Is Running From Trump Enough to Save Republicans on Tuesday?

sentences.en: For the past few months, my colleague, daily producer Caitlin O'Keefe, has been calling up voters across Maine to hear how they're feeling ahead of Tuesday's election.
sentences.zh: 在过去几个月里，我的同事、日常节目制作人凯特琳·奥基夫一直在给缅因州各地的选民打电话，了解他们在周二选举前的感受。

sentences.en: Recently, she spoke to a voter named David Bessie.
sentences.zh: 最近，她采访了一位名叫大卫·贝西的选民。

sentences.en: Can you just tell me how long you have lived in Maine for?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我你在缅因州住了多久吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: We have been here for three years.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里已经三年了。

sentences.en: I grew up in Waterville, Maine, and now my wife and I have retired back to my home state.
sentences.zh: 我在缅因州沃特维尔长大，现在我和妻子退休后回到了我的家乡。

sentences.en: Tell me like a little bit about your political identity.
sentences.zh: 跟我聊聊你的政治身份。

sentences.en: Is there a political party that you've historically identified with?
sentences.zh: 历史上有没有哪个政党是你一直认同的？

sentences.en: Yeah, I consider myself an anti-Magna Republican.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为自己是一个反MAGA的共和党人。

sentences.en: I think that I am generally more right of center in my political views.
sentences.zh: 我认为我的政治观点总体上更偏向右翼。

sentences.en: But I think that Trump and the Trump presidency, both Trump one and two, has been an absolute disaster for the country.
sentences.zh: 但我认为特朗普和特朗普的总统任期，无论是特朗普第一任期还是第二任期，对国家来说都是一场彻头彻尾的灾难。

sentences.en: I think the party is corrupt and self-dealing and honestly incompetent.
sentences.zh: 我认为这个党派是腐败的、谋取私利的，老实说也是无能的。

sentences.en: I think that the whole doge viasco was a missed opportunity to really make a difference.
sentences.zh: 我认为整个政府效率部闹剧是一个真正做出改变的错失良机。

sentences.en: And I think that the immigration and ICE, how that has evolved under this presidency, has been horrible.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为移民和移民及海关执法局，在这次总统任期内的演变情况，简直糟透了。

sentences.en: But I'm not a Democrat.
sentences.zh: 但我不是民主党人。

sentences.en: I think that the Democrats under Biden especially really followed what amounted to an open borders policy.
sentences.zh: 我认为民主党人，尤其是拜登领导下的民主党人，真的遵循了相当于开放边境的政策。

sentences.en: I think that the influence of unions on the Democratic Party is not a positive thing.
sentences.zh: 我认为工会对民主党的影响不是一件积极的事情。

sentences.en: I think that the Democrats kind of failed Economics 101 in general.
sentences.zh: 我认为民主党人基本上有点没及格经济学101。

sentences.en: They think that spending money is going to solve problems rather than trying to solve the problems and then think about money afterwards.
sentences.zh: 他们认为花钱就能解决问题，而不是先想办法解决问题，然后再考虑钱的事。

sentences.en: And it just seems goofy to me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说简直太荒谬了。

sentences.en: I can't wrap my head around why anybody would think that would be a logical thing to do.
sentences.zh: 我无法理解为什么会有人认为那是合乎逻辑的做法。

sentences.en: And the Democratic Party, and it feels like it's, if anything, it's veering more to the left rather than to the center, where I wish they would go.
sentences.zh: 而且民主党，如果说有什么不同的话，那就是它不仅没有走向我希望他们去的中心，反而感觉更向左倾斜了。

sentences.en: Well, it kind of brings us to this Senate race and why I'm struggling as much as I am with it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这就把我们带到了这场参议院竞选，以及我为什么为此如此纠结。

sentences.en: I think that Troy Jackson is really a standard liberal Democrat who's going to fall in line with the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 我认为特洛伊·杰克逊确实是一个标准的自由派民主党人，他会听从民主党的话。

sentences.en: Susan Collins, on the other hand, you know, she's consistently rated one of the senators who's willing to cross the aisle.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，你知道，苏珊·柯林斯一直被评为愿意跨越党派界限的参议员之一。

sentences.en: I look at Susan Collins' record, and it seems to me to be pretty solid and thoughtful.
sentences.zh: 我看了苏珊·柯林斯的记录，在我看来相当扎实和深思熟虑。

sentences.en: But I think that a vote for Susan Collins has the potential to help the MAGA Republican cohort.
sentences.zh: 但我认为投票给苏珊·柯林斯有可能帮助MAGA共和党人集团。

sentences.en: Part of the criticism of her is that she has not done everything that she could to try to stymie the Trump MAGA presidency.
sentences.zh: 对她的批评之一是，她没有尽其所能去阻挠特朗普的MAGA总统任期。

sentences.en: And, you know, that's probably true.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这可能是真的。

sentences.en: Could she have not voted for some of the nominations that have been made?
sentences.zh: 她难道就不能对提出的一些提名投反对票吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全可以。

sentences.en: I'll tell you my dream scenario.
sentences.zh: 我来告诉你我的梦想场景。

sentences.en: My dream scenario is that it's 50-50 in the Senate with Susan Collins still there.
sentences.zh: 我的梦想场景是参议院势均力敌，苏珊·柯林斯依然在那里。

sentences.en: So that things that need to get passed, she would be an important swing vote on.
sentences.zh: 这样对于需要通过的事情，她将成为一个重要的摇摆票。

sentences.en: Because I think she would be a swing vote and would be willing to vote down things that didn't make sense to her from the Republican side
sentences.zh: 因为我认为她会是一张摇摆票，并且愿意投票否决那些从共和党角度来看对她来说不合理的法案

sentences.en: and would be willing to vote for things on the Democratic side that did.
sentences.zh: 并且愿意对民主党方面合理的法案投赞成票。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: In this year's midterm elections, a very specific kind of Republican candidate is appealing to disillusioned voters of both parties.
sentences.zh: 在今年的中期选举中，一种非常特定类型的共和党候选人正在吸引两党幻灭的选民。

sentences.en: Moderates willing to openly criticize President Trump.
sentences.zh: 愿意公开批评特朗普总统的温和派。

sentences.en: The question now is whether running away from Trump and his unpopularity is enough to actually win.
sentences.zh: 现在的问题是，与特朗普及其不受欢迎保持距离是否足以真正赢得胜利。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague, Jess Bidgood, explains how some Republicans are trying to bring back an older version of the GOP as the future of their party.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事杰斯·比德古德解释了某些共和党人如何试图恢复老版本的共和党作为他们党派的未来。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, October 28th.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月28日星期三。

sentences.en: All right, are you ready?
sentences.zh: 好了，准备好了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 准备好了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Jess, really glad to have you here.
sentences.zh: 杰斯，很高兴你能来。

sentences.en: It's a delight to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: Delighted to have you here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能来。

sentences.en: So, in our study of Republicans who are defying political gravity in this midterm when so many things are not going well for the Republican Party,
sentences.zh: 那么，在我们研究那些在这个共和党遭遇重重困难的中期选举中违背政治重力规律的共和党人时，

sentences.en: exhibit A, I think, has to be Susan Collins, who is neck and neck in the polls with her Democratic rival.
sentences.zh: 我认为典型的例子必须是苏珊·柯林斯，她在民调中与民主党对手不相上下。

sentences.en: In some polls, she's actually ahead of him.
sentences.zh: 在某些民调中，她实际上还领先于他。

sentences.en: In a state, Maine, where the Democrats have won the popular vote in the last at least three presidential races, I think even more than that.
sentences.zh: 在缅因州这样一个在过去至少三次总统大选中民主党都赢得了普选的州，我认为甚至还不止于此。

sentences.en: So, let's talk about how Susan Collins has done that.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们来谈谈苏珊·柯林斯是如何做到这一点的。

sentences.en: So, there's two things happening in Maine that I think explain this.
sentences.zh: 缅因州有两件事我认为可以解释这一点。

sentences.en: The first is Democrats, and the second is Susan Collins.
sentences.zh: 第一是民主党人，第二是苏珊·柯林斯。

sentences.en: So, let's talk about Democrats real quick.
sentences.zh: 那我们简单聊聊民主党人。

sentences.en: Let's just remind ourselves about the saga of Democrats in Maine this year.
sentences.zh: 让我们回想一下今年缅因州民主党的传奇故事。

sentences.en: Saga it was.
sentences.zh: 确实是个传奇。

sentences.en: Going into this year, Chuck Schumer had an idea about who he thought could take down Susan Collins because she is somebody who Democrats have wanted to beat.
sentences.zh: 进入今年，查克·舒默对谁能击败苏珊·柯林斯有了一个想法，因为她是民主党人一直想要击败的人。

sentences.en: They have been hungry to beat Susan Collins for decades.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，他们一直渴望击败苏珊·柯林斯。

sentences.en: And he looked at the sitting governor of Maine, Janet Mills, who has won twice in that state, and said she can do it.
sentences.zh: 他看中了缅因州现任州长珍妮特·米尔斯，她在该州赢得过两次竞选，并说她能做到。

sentences.en: Maine voters did not agree.
sentences.zh: 缅因州选民并不同意。

sentences.en: Instead, they got really excited about an oysterman who came out of nowhere named Graham Plattner.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们对一个不知从哪里冒出来的名叫格雷厄姆·普拉特纳的养蚝人感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: We've talked a lot about this.
sentences.zh: 我们已经讨论过很多次了。

sentences.en: We sure have.
sentences.zh: 我们当然讨论过。

sentences.en: In recent months.
sentences.zh: 在最近几个月里。

sentences.en: His candidacy.
sentences.zh: 他的候选人资格。

sentences.en: Implodes.
sentences.zh: 崩塌了。

sentences.en: Implodes after he is accused of rape, and Democrats have to scramble to find somebody else, and they find Troy Jackson, who is a former Senate president in Maine,
sentences.zh: 在他被指控强奸后崩塌了，民主党人不得不争先恐后地寻找其他人，他们找到了特洛伊·杰克逊，他曾任缅因州参议院议长，

sentences.en: not someone who has ever won statewide.
sentences.zh: 并不是那种曾经在全州范围内赢得过竞选的人。

sentences.en: In fact, I don't think he's ever won an election with more than 10 or 11,000 votes.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我认为他从未赢得过得票超过1万或1.1万票的选举。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And as our colleagues, including Nate Cohn, have found clever ways to say, he has a charisma deficit.
sentences.zh: 正如我们的同事（包括内特·科恩）用巧妙的方式发现的那样，他存在魅力赤字。

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And then, of course, there's another reason why Maine is so much tougher for Democrats than they would like.
sentences.zh: 当然，缅因州对民主党人来说比他们希望的要艰难得多，还有另一个原因。

sentences.en: And that is a big old story about Susan Collins herself.
sentences.zh: 那就是关于苏珊·柯林斯本人的宏大故事。

sentences.en: She has really placed a bet that her brand of independent, fairly moderate Republicanism, one that predates Trump by literally decades, is the one that will meet the moment today.
sentences.zh: 她确实下注认为，她那种独立、相当温和的共和党主义品牌——比特朗普早了整整几十年——才是能够应对当今时代的选择。

sentences.en: Jess, just remind us of this Susan Collins, old-school brand of Republicanism.
sentences.zh: 杰斯，请提醒我们苏珊·柯林斯这种老派的共和党主义品牌。

sentences.en: Susan Collins was first elected to the Senate in 1996.
sentences.zh: 苏珊·柯林斯于1996年首次当选参议员。

sentences.en: And it will be service to the people of my state that will be my highest priority as Maine's newest senator.
sentences.zh: 作为缅因州最新的参议员，为我州人民服务将是我最高的工作优先级。

sentences.en: She is somebody who likes the nuts and bolts of governance.
sentences.zh: 她是一个喜欢治理国家细枝末节的人。

sentences.en: She has risen to be chairwoman of the Appropriations Committee.
sentences.zh: 她已经晋升为拨款委员会主席。

sentences.en: This is about as wonky as government gets.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是政府中最务实的领域了。

sentences.en: I've secured money for the University of Maine, which just this last week has translated into a new manufacturing plant in Bangor that will produce 75 good-paying jobs.
sentences.zh: 我为缅因大学争取到了资金，就在上周，这些资金已经转化为班戈的一家新制造厂，将提供75个待遇优厚的工作岗位。

sentences.en: And Susan Collins has really forged an identity for herself as somebody who brings home the bacon to Maine.
sentences.zh: 苏珊·柯林斯确实为自己树立了一种身份，即一个能为缅因州带回实际利益的人。

sentences.en: So I'm going to continue advocating tax incentives to encourage small businesses to create jobs and supporting local economic development efforts all over this state.
sentences.zh: 因此，我将继续倡导税收优惠以鼓励小企业创造就业机会，并支持全州范围内的本地经济发展努力。

sentences.en: This is an old-fashioned form of governance, right?
sentences.zh: 这是一种老式的治理形式，对吧？

sentences.en: This is not flashy.
sentences.zh: 这并不张扬。

sentences.en: This is not going on Fox News and saying stuff that gets super viral.
sentences.zh: 这不是去福克斯新闻说那些能引起病毒式传播的话。

sentences.en: Hand in hand with that was an identity as a kind of bipartisan person.
sentences.zh: 与此相辅相成的是她作为一种两党合作人物的身份。

sentences.en: I've always worked across party lines.
sentences.zh: 我一直在跨越党派界限工作。

sentences.en: That has been the hallmark of my service in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 那一直是我在参议院服务的标志。

sentences.en: That's what I'm known for.
sentences.zh: 这就是我为人所知的原因。

sentences.en: And that was something that was really seen as a selling point.
sentences.zh: 而这确实被视为一个卖点。

sentences.en: And because of my ability to work across party lines, I have a long record of legislative accomplishment in a host of issues, whether it's homeless.
sentences.zh: 由于我能够跨越党派界限工作，我在一系列问题上拥有长期的立法成就记录，无论是无家可归者问题。

sentences.en: And this was an identity and a brand that she was building for herself for 20 years before Trump comes down the escalator and bursts onto the scene.
sentences.zh: 这是她在特朗普走下自动扶梯并登上政坛之前20年里一直在为自己塑造的身份和品牌。

sentences.en: And how does Collins handle the arrival of Trump, who is, by the time he's president, ferociously partisan, but also quite punitive to those who want to work with the other side?
sentences.zh: 柯林斯如何应对特朗普的到来？当特朗普成为总统时，他极具党派偏见，而且对那些想要与另一方合作的人相当惩罚性。

sentences.en: It results in him often saying, you just betrayed me and I will now make sure you're no longer a member of Congress.
sentences.zh: 这导致他经常说，你背叛了我，我现在要确保你不再是国会议员。

sentences.en: Susan Collins has often worked to maintain as much distance from President Trump as she can have.
sentences.zh: 苏珊·柯林斯经常努力与特朗普总统保持尽可能多的距离。

sentences.en: I don't think that President Trump is going to come to Maine, and I'm not exactly his favorite senator.
sentences.zh: 我不认为特朗普总统会来缅因州，我也不是他最喜欢的参议员。

sentences.en: She is well aware that Maine is a place that has voted for Trump's opponents when presidential elections roll around every time.
sentences.zh: 她很清楚，每当总统大选来临时，缅因州每次都会投票给特朗普的对手。

sentences.en: I decide my votes on what I believe is best for Maine and for America.
sentences.zh: 我根据我认为对缅因州和对美国最好的结果来决定我的投票。

sentences.en: Not on whether or not any president, and I've worked with five, is for it or against it.
sentences.zh: 而不是基于任何总统——我共事过五位——是赞成还是反对。

sentences.en: And so, more than any other Republican senator over the past decade, she has broken with her party during votes on Capitol Hill.
sentences.zh: 因此，在过去的十年里，她比任何其他共和党参议员都更经常在国会山的投票中与她的党派分道扬镳。

sentences.en: I vote very independently.
sentences.zh: 我投票非常独立。

sentences.en: And that is something that she is drawing on now as she runs for re-election in this moment when President Trump's approval ratings are in the 30s.
sentences.zh: 这就是她现在竞选连任时所依赖的东西，当时特朗普总统的支持率在30%左右。

sentences.en: Her party is facing strong national headwinds, probably as strong as she has ever faced when running for re-election.
sentences.zh: 她的党派面临着强大的国家逆风，这可能是她在竞选连任时面临的最强大的逆风。

sentences.en: I have been extremely outspoken in my opposition to Canadian tariffs, and I have voted repeatedly to repeal them.
